annotation_description: Playing Ancient Tomb on turn 1 produces 2 colorless mana with nothing useful to cast, while Flooded Strand could fetch an Island to cast Ponder, digging for red sources and setting up the Sneak Attack game plan. The turn is essentially wasted.

Chalice of the Void on X=0 is far less impactful than Chalice on X=1 in Legacy against a blue deck running Ponder, Force of Will, and other 1-mana spells. The opponent's deck likely has few or no 0-mana spells, making Chalice on 0 nearly worthless, while Chalice on 1 would shut down a huge portion of their game plan. City of Traitors produces exactly {C}{C} which pays for Chalice on either 0 or 1.

The player already has City of Traitors producing 2 colorless mana. They have a second Chalice of the Void in hand. With City of Traitors providing {C}{C}, they could cast Chalice of the Void for X=1, which would be devastating against the opponent who likely runs many 1-mana spells (Ponder, Force of Will when hardcast costs 5 but the deck likely has Brainstorm, Swords to Plowshares, etc. in a Legacy blue deck). They already have Chalice on 0 from a previous play. Deploying Chalice on 1 would lock out a huge portion of Legacy blue decks' cantrips. Instead, the player passed without casting anything, saving mana for unclear future plans. The reasoning about not playing Mountain to preserve City of Traitors is correct, but they failed to consider using the available 2 mana from City of Traitors to deploy the second Chalice at X=1.

message: Select a Plains or Island card
annotation_description: Fetching basic Island provides no red mana, which is essential for casting Sneak Attack (3R). The hand's primary game plan revolves around Sneak Attack, and without a red source, it becomes uncastable without drawing additional lands. Volcanic Island would provide both blue and red mana.

Playing Mountain sacrifices City of Traitors, leaving only 1 mana source next turn. This prevents casting Blood Moon ({2}{R}) on turn 3 without burning Simian Spirit Guide. By waiting to play Mountain until turn 3, they could have City of Traitors (2 colorless) + Mountain (1 red) = exactly {2}{R} for Blood Moon, which would lock the opponent's Ancient Tomb into a Mountain.

Failed to play Mountain and cast Blood Moon on turn 2. With Mountain (land drop) + City of Traitors (2 colorless) + Simian Spirit Guide (exile for R), Johnny had exactly the mana to cast Blood Moon ({2}{R}), which would turn the opponent's Ancient Tomb into a Mountain and severely cripple their mana development. Instead, Johnny passed without even playing a land, confused about the game state.

Playing Mountain causes City of Traitors to be sacrificed before its mana can be used to cast Blood Moon. This wastes the turn's mana and delays the devastating Blood Moon by at least a turn, giving the opponent time to develop their board.

Playing Mountain causes City of Traitors to be sacrificed, losing 2 colorless mana production. The player already has two Chalices on the battlefield (presumably at 0 and 1, locking out the opponent's cheap spells). With City of Traitors providing {C}{C}, the player could have tapped City of Traitors for mana first to cast Blood Moon (using City of Traitors {C}{C} + exile Simian Spirit Guide for {R} = 3 mana) BEFORE playing the Mountain. Blood Moon would turn the opponent's Ancient Tombs into Mountains (neutering their mana) while keeping City of Traitors alive since no new land was played yet. Instead, playing Mountain first sacrificed City of Traitors for free, losing a critical mana source. Even if they wanted to play Mountain eventually, they should have cast Blood Moon first using City of Traitors mana, then played Mountain afterward (City would sacrifice but Blood Moon would already be on the battlefield).

Evoking Fury when the opponent has no creatures or planeswalkers on the battlefield wastes Fury and the red card exiled to pay for evoke, dealing 4 damage to nothing meaningful. The ETB trigger requires targeting creatures and/or planeswalkers, and there are none on the opponent's side.

Evoking Fury when the opponent has no creatures or planeswalkers on the battlefield wastes Fury and the exiled red card for essentially no value. Fury's ETB deals damage only to creatures/planeswalkers, not players, so the 4 damage goes to waste. This throws away two red cards (Fury + the exiled card) that could be critical later.

Gem25F Johnny already has a Chalice of the Void on 0 counters in play from turn 1. Casting a second Chalice on X=0 is completely redundant - it adds no new coverage since the first Chalice already counters all 0-mana spells. This wastes a card that could have been cast on a different X value (like X=2) to counter important spells like Stock Up or other 2-mana spells the opponent might have. With only 1 Mountain, casting Chalice on X=0 costs 0 mana, but casting it on any other value requires more mana. However, the card is still wasted for no effect when it could have been held for a future turn when more mana is available to set it at a meaningful value like X=2 or X=3.

Qwen3 passed the turn with 5 available mana and multiple castable spells. Stock Up (MV 3, not countered by either Chalice) could be cast for 2U using Ancient Tomb + Volcanic Island, digging 5 deep for 2 cards to find creatures for Sneak Attack or additional resources. Passing wastes an entire turn of development against an opponent with lock pieces.

Passed the turn without casting any spells despite having castable Stock Up (MV 3, dodges both Chalices) that could dig for creatures to pair with Sneak Attack. Ancient Tomb + Volcanic Island provides exactly 2U for Stock Up. With no pressure from opponent and a hand full of expensive cards needing setup, failing to dig is a significant missed opportunity.

Passed the turn with 6 available mana and multiple castable spells. Stock Up (costing {2}{U}) would dig 5 cards deep to find creatures for the Sneak Attack game plan, and Sneak Attack itself could be deployed. The opponent has minimal board presence (just Chalices and a Mountain), so there's little reason to hold up Force of Will over developing the board. Wasting an entire turn of mana when trying to assemble a combo is a significant tempo loss.

Player had the line of playing City of Traitors then casting Blood Moon or Magus of the Moon (City provides 2 colorless + Mountain provides 1 red = exactly 2R) to turn all opponent's nonbasic lands into Mountains, severely hampering their mana while Sneak Attack is their key threat. Instead, the player appears to have misunderstood City of Traitors (thinking it sacrifices existing lands) and likely chose Fury, which has no meaningful targets on the board (Fury's ETB only hits creatures/planeswalkers).

Blood Moon converts opponent's Ancient Tombs into Mountains that produce {R}, making it easier to activate Sneak Attack (which only costs {R}). While it does shut off Boseiju's channel ability, the opponent already has Volcanic Island for red mana. With Sneak Attack already on board, pressuring the opponent's 11 life total may be more urgent than land disruption.

With Blood Moon already on the battlefield, the player passed without casting anything. They could have exiled Simian Spirit Guide for R, giving RRR total, and cast Broadside Bombardiers (a 2/2 with menace and haste) to apply pressure against an opponent at 11 life who has Sneak Attack threatening to come online. The player's reasoning was confused, thinking they were waiting for mana payment on Magus of the Moon, but this was actually a fresh casting decision.

Failed to activate Sneak Attack with Atraxa, Grand Unifier in hand. With Blood Moon turning all lands into Mountains, Qwen3 has plenty of {R} available. Sneaking Atraxa would trigger its powerful ETB (revealing top 10, drawing up to one card per type), attack for 7 with flying/lifelink (gaining crucial life from 11 back to 18), and deal 7 damage to the opponent. This is the deck's primary game plan.

Qwen3 Vorthos has Sneak Attack on the battlefield and Atraxa, Grand Unifier in hand with plenty of red mana available (all lands are Mountains due to Blood Moon). Activating Sneak Attack to put Atraxa into play would trigger her ETB to reveal top 10 cards and potentially add up to 8 cards to hand across different card types, plus gain 7 life from lifelink if she could attack (though this is post-combat). Even without attacking, the ETB alone is game-changingly powerful. At 11 life against an opponent with Blood Moon and Chalice lock pieces, this card advantage injection could be the difference between winning and losing.

Blood Moon is already on the battlefield making all nonbasic lands Mountains. Casting Magus of the Moon provides a completely redundant effect. The only value is a 2/2 body without haste, while Broadside Bombardiers would provide a 2/2 with haste and menace that can attack immediately and has a powerful boast ability.
Magus of the Moon is completely redundant with Blood Moon already on the battlefield — it adds no new effect beyond being a vanilla 2/2 body. The opponent's nonbasic lands are already Mountains.

Magus of the Moon is completely redundant with Blood Moon already on the battlefield. Meanwhile, Fury could be hardcast (using lands + Simian Spirit Guide exile) as a 3/3 double striker representing 6 damage per turn, creating a 2-turn clock against the opponent at 11 life.

With 6 mana available (2 Mountains + 2 City of Traitors) and the opponent at 11 life, casting Simian Spirit Guide as a vanilla 2/2 for 3 mana is far inferior to casting Pyrogoyf for 4 mana. The graveyard contains multiple card types (artifact from Chalice, enchantment from Blood Moon, creature from Magus, land from City of Traitors, sorcery from opponent's Ponder, instant from Lotus Petal) making Pyrogoyf approximately a 5/6 or larger that also deals its power as damage to any target on ETB - potentially dealing 5+ damage directly to the opponent who is at 11 life.

With 5 red mana available (3 Mountains + 2 City of Traitors turned to Mountains by Blood Moon), casting Simian Spirit Guide as a vanilla 2/2 instead of Pyrogoyf which would be a 5/6 (5 card types in graveyards) AND deal 5 damage to the opponent on ETB (dropping them from 11 to 6 life) is a massive missed opportunity. The opponent has Sneak Attack active and could end the game at any moment, so maximizing damage output is critical.

With Blood Moon/Magus making all lands Mountains (3 R available), exiling Simian Spirit Guide would provide a 4th mana to cast The One Ring, which is a significantly more impactful play than Broadside Bombardiers. The One Ring provides protection from everything for the turn (critical with opponent's Sneak Attack threatening huge creatures), indestructibility, and card advantage engine. Broadside Bombardiers is a 2/2 that's relatively low-impact.

The opponent has Sneak Attack on the battlefield, which is an extremely dangerous threat. The One Ring was castable (3 lands + exile Simian Spirit Guide = 4 mana) and would have provided protection from everything until next turn, shutting down any Sneak Attack activations, while also providing a card draw engine. Instead, a 2/2 haste creature was deployed that applies minimal pressure.

Under Blood Moon, all three land options (Wasteland, Cavern of Souls, Eye of Ugin) would enter as Mountains tapping for {R}. There's no downside to playing one, and the extra mana source provides flexibility, especially with Sneak Attack on board needing {R} activations to put Atraxa into play.

Declined to play a land when holding three lands (Wasteland, Cavern of Souls, Eye of Ugin). Under Blood Moon, all would enter as Mountains providing {R}. There's no downside to playing any of them, and the extra mana source could be relevant for multiple Sneak Attack activations or casting spells.

Opponent is at 9 life with Blood Moon already in play making Magus of the Moon redundant. Broadside Bombardiers' Boast ability could sacrifice Magus of the Moon to deal 5 damage (2 + CMC 3), putting opponent to 4 life. This is essentially free damage since Blood Moon already maintains the nonbasic-lands-are-Mountains lock.

Veil of Summer (MV 1) is permanently dead while Chalice of the Void on 1 is in play - it will always be countered. Stock Up could become castable if Blood Moon is removed (e.g., by channeling Boseiju to destroy it), after which Volcanic Islands would produce blue mana again.

Player has lethal on board: attack with Magus of the Moon (2) + Broadside Bombardiers (2) for 4 damage (opponent to 5), then use Bombardiers' Boast to sacrifice Magus of the Moon (CMC 3) dealing 2+3=5 damage for exact lethal. The player's reasoning shows no awareness of this lethal line, focusing instead on incremental value plays. Playing Urza's Saga first is fine, but only if they follow up with the lethal attack.

Missed lethal. Pyrogoyf's ETB deals damage equal to its power (6, based on ~6 card types in graveyards) to any target, which could target the opponent at 9 life. Combined with attacking with Magus of the Moon (2) and Broadside Bombardiers (2), that's 10 damage total against 9 life. Instead, chose to play Urza's Saga which becomes a basic Mountain under Blood Moon and does nothing.

Johnny missed lethal damage this turn. Broadside Bombardiers can attack (2 damage, opponent to 7), then use Boast to sacrifice Magus of the Moon (CMC 3) dealing 2+3=5 damage to opponent (down to 2), then cast Pyrogoyf for 4 mana (available from 2x City of Traitors + Mountain). Pyrogoyf's ETB deals damage equal to its power (at least 5 given card types in graveyards: land, artifact, enchantment, sorcery, instant) to any target, killing the opponent. Instead, Johnny cast The One Ring which doesn't advance the kill.

Missed lethal. Opponent is at 9 life with no blockers. Pyrogoyf (costs {3}{R}, payable with City of Traitors x2 + Mountain or Simian Spirit Guide) enters as a 6-power creature (6 card types in graveyards: land, artifact, enchantment, creature, sorcery, instant) and its ETB deals 6 damage to the opponent. Then attacking with Broadside Bombardiers (2 menace) and Magus of the Moon (2) deals 4 more combat damage, totaling 10 damage against 9 life.

Broadside Bombardiers attacked this turn, enabling its Boast ability. Sacrificing Magus of the Moon (CMC 3) to the Boast would deal 2+3=5 damage directly to the opponent at 7 life, bringing them to 2. Instead, the player appears to be casting Simian Spirit Guide as a vanilla 2/2, completely ignoring a powerful activated ability that nearly delivers lethal damage.

Missed lethal. Broadside Bombardiers attacked this turn, enabling its Boast ability. Evoking Fury (exile a red card like Pyrogoyf) then using Bombardiers' Boast to sacrifice Fury deals 2 + 5 (Fury's mana value) = 7 damage to opponent at exactly 7 life, which is lethal.

At 7 life with Pyrogoyf on the stack (which will deal 6 damage on ETB), Qwen3 Vorthos activated Sneak Attack instead of countering with Force of Will. Sneak Attack putting Atraxa into play doesn't prevent the 6 ETB damage from Pyrogoyf, and since it's postcombat main, Atraxa can't even attack before being sacrificed at end step. This leaves them at 1 life in a desperate position instead of safely at 7.

Pyrogoyf's ETB trigger will deal 6 damage (6 card types in graveyards) targeting Qwen3 Vorthos, dropping them from 7 to 1 life. At 1 life with opponent having Broadside Bombardiers (which can sacrifice creatures for direct damage) and Magus of the Moon on board, Qwen3 is essentially dead. Force of Will could counter the Pyrogoyf, preventing it from entering and avoiding the lethal ETB trigger entirely.
